name: IXL
line: IXL practices one chosen skill at a time. In AMP, every answer sets the next problem, and learned skills come back.
description: AMP vs IXL: IXL practices one chosen skill at a time toward a SmartScore. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: IXL organizes practice by skill: the learner or an adult opens a skill, and a SmartScore of 100 marks it mastered [2][6]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem. IXL measures in two places: a separate diagnostic, LevelUp, whose math benchmark takes about 45 minutes [7], and the SmartScore, which tracks one skill at a time [2].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In IXL the unit is the skill. A right answer brings a similar or slightly harder question in the same skill [5]. Inside a skill, feedback comes after a wrong answer, as a step-by-step explanation of the correct one [4]. IXL's written lessons cover grade 3 through Geometry [9]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [23].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP every answer sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. Repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. In IXL the learner or an adult opens a skill, from a grade list, from IXL's recommendations, or from skills a parent stars [6][10], and every grade level is open [11]. Recommendations can point to building-block skills for a trouble spot, and IXL presents them as options for students to explore [6].

reasons.title: What counts as learned
reasons.body: In AMP a skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once. An answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped and does not count as learned. IXL marks a skill mastered at a SmartScore of 100. The score rises on right answers and falls on wrong ones, by a formula IXL calls proprietary, and its gains taper off near the top [2][5]. From 90 on, the questions are the hardest in the skill [3]. AMP's rule is open source: open to peer review and contribution.

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. IXL practice stays inside one skill [5], and we found no scheduled review of mastered skills in the help articles and design paper we read [5][6]. IXL's own researchers have studied spacing among students who spaced their practice on their own [21]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [22].

rows.range: Pre-K through Calculus, plus Integrated Math 1 to 3, with skills listed by grade and course [1].
rows.start: A separate diagnostic, LevelUp. Its math benchmark takes about 45 minutes [7]. Or the learner opens any skill at any grade [11].
rows.teaching: A step-by-step explanation of the correct answer after a wrong one [4]. Written lessons for grade 3 through Geometry [9].
rows.next: The learner or an adult picks a skill. Recommendations suggest skills, including building-block skills for trouble spots [6].
rows.mastery: A SmartScore of 100. It rises on right answers and falls on wrong ones, by a formula IXL calls proprietary [2].
rows.review: No scheduled review of mastered skills found in the help articles and design paper we read [5][6]. Practice stays inside one skill [5].
rows.print: IXL calls its practice an interactive worksheet. For paper, it points to its printed workbooks [12].
rows.adult: Stars skills for a child [10]. Teachers can set SmartScore goals [13]. IXL says it reinforces concepts introduced in a learner's lessons [14].
rows.reports: Teacher reports include a questions log, with the student's iPad scratchpad work [15].
rows.evidence: One randomized trial: +0.13 SD on Star Math, +0.03 (not significant) on the state test [16]. Rated Strong by Evidence for ESSA [17].

theirs: IXL comes from IXL Learning. IXL Math runs from Pre-K through Calculus, with its skills listed by grade and course [1]. IXL calls its practice an interactive worksheet [12], and it offers a separate diagnostic, LevelUp [7].

A learner opens a skill: from a grade list, from IXL's recommendations, or from skills a parent or teacher has starred [6][10]. Questions come one at a time and are marked at once [12]. A right answer brings a similar or slightly harder question; a wrong one brings an explanation [4][5]. A SmartScore from 0 to 100 tracks the skill. 80 is proficient, 90 opens the Challenge Zone of the hardest questions, and 100 is mastered [2][3].
credit: Every answer is marked at once, and a wrong one brings a step-by-step explanation of the correct answer [4][12].
It has been studied in a randomized trial run by researchers at Johns Hopkins University [16].

theirs: IXL's strongest study is a randomized trial run by the Center for Research and Reform in Education at Johns Hopkins University, which contracted with IXL Learning to do it [16]. In spring 2023, classes in four elementary schools in Holland, Michigan, were randomly assigned to use IXL Math or not: 545 students in grades 3 to 5. Students used it for about 10 hours in grade 3 and 7 to 8 hours in grades 4 and 5 over the semester. IXL classes gained 0.13 standard deviations more on Star Math, a significant result. On Michigan's state test, M-STEP, the difference was 0.03 and not statistically significant [16].

Evidence for ESSA rates IXL Math Strong, based on this one randomized study of 545 students in grades 3 to 5, with an average effect size of +0.08 [17]. The same Johns Hopkins center runs Evidence for ESSA [17].

Most of IXL's other research is its own [18]. A 2019 IXL study in one virtual charter school matched about 3,000 users with similar non-users over a semester and found 0.05 standard deviations on MAP; its larger headline number is for students who mastered 25 or more skills [19]. A three-year Oklahoma study by an IXL researcher counted a school as an IXL school if at least 10% of its students used IXL Math, and reports 0.23 on school proficiency rates, an effect the author says should be read at the school level, not the student level [20]. Neither study assigned IXL at random.
ours: The two findings that bear on this comparison: in a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed and spaced math practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [22], and worked examples improve math performance across 55 studies [23]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: You want to pick each skill and practice it on its own until a score marks it mastered.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want the program to choose every next problem, and to go back to what a skill builds on.
You want a hint and a lesson with a worked example at every problem, before the answer.
You want learned skills to keep coming back, mixed with other math.
You want printed workbooks made from your child's own work, with worked answer keys.

questions.question: How is AMP different from IXL?
questions.answer: In IXL the learner or an adult picks a skill, and a SmartScore of 100 marks it mastered [2][6]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does IXL work?
questions.answer: One randomized trial, run by Johns Hopkins University researchers under contract with IXL Learning, found IXL classes gained 0.13 standard deviations on Star Math over a semester, and 0.03, not statistically significant, on Michigan's state test [16]. Evidence for ESSA rates IXL Math Strong on that study [17]. Most of IXL's other studies are its own [18].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
